title: Testing an app offline and on a poor connection

videos.script: Every test in this course so far ran on a perfect network. The app and boxoffice were on the same computer, and every answer came back in milliseconds. {{perfect}} The person holding the phone is on a train. The signal drops in a tunnel, comes back slowly, and drops again. {{train}} A bad network is not one failure. It is a slow answer, a thin one, an answer that never comes, and a connection that comes and goes. {{kinds}} And the worst of them is invisible. The request arrived, the order was made, and only the answer was lost on the way back. {{lost}} In this lesson you build that network yourself. A small proxy in Node that sits in front of boxoffice and spoils its answers on purpose. {{proxy}} You watch what it does to curl, to boxoffice's own call to the payment provider, and to a client that retries. {{effects}} Then the app. How to take the network away from the emulator, what Tickets shows when it does, and a test that puts the slow proxy between them. {{app}} And last, what such a test should assert, so that a bad network is something you test rather than something you hope for. {{assert}}
